findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
The following canned foods on the dry shelves were observed to have dents:
1. Hunts pasta sauce has significant dents on the body and along the seam (x6).
2. Sweetened condensed filled milk has dent along the seam.
3. Campbell chunky clam chowder has significant dents on the body (x2).
4. Campbell spicy tomato soup has significant dent on the body.
5. Boiled peanuts has dent along the seam.

CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and educated and the dented cans were removed from the shelves. Dented cans can have entry and harborage of botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelves and not sold to customers.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometer was observed in the cooler across the women’s restroom. The PIC was informed, educated and instructed to provide internal thermometer in the cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure an ambient thermometer is placed in the warmest part of the cooler to accurately monitor internal temperature.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Dead ants were observed on the floor at the far left end corners close to the brown door, under the electrical equipments in the back storage. The PIC was instructed by the inspector to have the dead ants removed from the facility and the floor area cleaned. Ensure the dead insects are removed from the facility and the floor area is cleaned to sight. The inspector will be back on April 10, 2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Light was observed to be passing beneath the door at the back storage. The PIC was informed, educated and advised to use weather stripping to seal the gap beneath the door. Ensure the gap is sealed to prevent potential entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Significant soil accumulations were observed on the external surfaces of the freezer doors at the back storage.
2. The first standing cooler across the women’s restroom was observed to have soil accumulation on the plastic holes at the bottom of the cooler door.

The PIC was instructed by the inspector to have those surfaces cleaned. Ensure the surfaces of the freezer and standing cooler mentioned above are cleaned and kept free of soil accumulations.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Dirty water and mop heads were observed in the mop bucket at the mop station and in a black bucket in the mop sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and educated on proper air-drying techniques for mop heads; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop heads were placed in the mop sink with the mop heads facing upwards to air-dry since there was no empty wringer basket or hanger. Ensure water from mopping is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Shelves under the chip baskets were observed soiled. Clean shelves.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors are dirty throughout the facility and in need of a deep clean. PIC said floors are due for an overnight deep clean in January. Maintain floors clean. Inspector will follow up at the next routine inspection. Ref. 6-501.12 [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-202.12 (C) Metered faucet in women’s restroom did not provide flowing water for at least 15 seconds. Hot water ran for 10 seconds, and cold water ran for 1 second. Store manager placed a work order for repairs during inspection. 
A self-closing, slow-closing, or metering faucet shall provide a flow of water for at least 15 seconds without the need to reactivate the faucet.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap was not available at the women’s restroom handwahsing sink. Soap was provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Dented cans were stocked and available for purchase. Foods included Hunts meat pasta sauce (24oz x 2); Campbell’s chicken noodle soup (13.8oz); and Utopia black olives (6oz). All damaged cans were removed to be wasted. 
Food packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Left water fountain was observed with a buildup of mold beneath the bubbler head and general buildup within the basin and at the drain. Left water fountain was observed with a slow, constant trickle of water but did not allow for full flow of water when the handle was pushed to dispense water. Water fountain was cleaned during inspection. Repair the left fountain to function properly or shut it off. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Old mop water was observed in a mop bucket in the mop closet. Store manager stated used mop water was not from the current operating day. Proper disposal of waste water was discussed, and soiled mop water was discarded.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in mop buckets as it may serve as a potential water source for pests.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
5-501.17 Women's room did not have a covered waste can. Provide at least one covered trash receptacle in the women's restroom.
A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12 Mopsink basin was soiled with buildup and blocked with various items, including used mop heads. Items were removed and mop sink was cleaned during inspection.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Damp, partially dried mop heads were observed in the mop sink and stored in the top compartment of the mop bucket. Proper storage of mops after use was discussed. Used mop heads were discarded.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Several dented cans, some severely dented along seams and/or with sharp dents in the middle of the can, were stocked and available for purchase. Foods included, but were not necessarily limited to the following: Hunts meat pasta sauce (24oz); StarKist chunk light tuna in water (5oz); Goya black beans (15.5oz); Bristol Brand lunch loaf (12oz x 2); Armour Vienna bites (10oz); Mother Maid cherry topping (15oz x2); and Pampa peach slices (15.25oz). All damaged cans were removed to be wasted. Store manager stated one person is currently responsible for stocking food and will be advised on the issue. 
Food packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Significant gap was observed under the double doors in the back of the building at the loading dock/storage area. Two photos were taken and shown to the manager. Store manager stated the doors were damaged late last year during a delivery, and the new doors still need some work. A work order has already been placed to get the doors properly sealed. 
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; providing closed, tight-fitting windows; and providing solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Water fountains back by the restrooms were observed to have moldy buildup in the basins around the drains. The left water fountain was observed with a slow, constant trickle of water but did not allow for full flow of water when the handle was pushed to dispense water. Clean the water fountains. Repair the left fountain to function properly.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Waste water was observed in one of the mop buckets in the mop closet. Proper disposal of waste water was discussed, and soiled mop water was discarded.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in mop buckets as it may serve as a potential water source for pests.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
5-501.17 Women's room did not have a covered waste can. Provide at least one covered trash receptacle in the women's restroom.
A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12 Mopsink basin was soiled with buildup. Also, the floor along the wall in the mop closet was soiled with buildup and general debris. Clean the mopsink and the floor in the mop closet as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Wet mops were observed with mop heads stored on the floor and in the mopsink. Proper storage of mops after use was discussed.  
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Dented cans were observed out for sale on shelves. Items included tomato soup (3), cream of mushroom soup (1), chili with beans (2), and corned beef and hash (1).  One can of jalapeno peppers was also observed to be dented and bulging on the top. All questionable canned goods were removed from sales floor and set aside to be damaged out. 

Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption. Check cans as they are stocked, and do not stock cans that are dented on the top/bottom/side seams, have sharp dents on any surface, or are bulging or appear questionable in any other way. Check the cans frequently and remove damaged/questionable products as needed.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - An intermittent leak was observed at the cap of the vacuum breaker on the mopsink when the water was turned on. Have a licensed plumber repair or replace the vacuum breaker.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120(d) - Handsinks in restrooms are automatic and do not provide the flow of water for at least 15 seconds. The women's room faucet stays on for ~8-10 seconds, and the men's room faucet stays on for less than 5 seconds. Manual faucets need to provide adequate water flow to allow for proper handwashing. Have a licensed plumber repair the faucets so they function properly and allow for proper handwashing. (See General Comments)

All self-closing, slow closing, or metering faucet used shall be designed to provide a flow of water for at least 15 seconds without the need to reactivate the faucet.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690: The reach-in display freezers continue to have approximately two inches of frost accumulation. Defrost the freezers so they are smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The handsinks in the toilet rooms have a gap between them and the wall. Eliminate gap - caulk and smooth. Also, the majority of the reach-in freezers are observed with about an inch to two inches of frost accumulation. Defrost the reach-in freezers so that surfaces are maintained smooth and easily cleanable. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 The toilet papers, towels, cups etc available for customers are observed stored on the floor. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 There is a sizeable gap between the two front doors (widens towards the bottom). Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.
